digest.component_or_area: store write lock acquisition and retry logic
propositions: A write whose lock acquire times out is permanently discarded with no retry or queue, making the budget terminal and lossy rather than a fairness mechanism

Bounded retry-with-backoff converts lock-acquisition timeouts into latency instead of data loss, with backoff schedule 0.5s / 1.0s / capped 2.0s between passes and ~181.5s total ceiling (3 passes × 60s + backoff)
Retry is safe without phantom-write semantics because it lives strictly inside acquire() before the caller's write body runs, so LockTimeout is raised before any event is staged or committed

Five call sites opt into retries via REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env var (default 2, clamped 0-10): three in event_append.py, one each in txn.py and push.py; all other callers keep fail-fast through retries=0 default
Holder-duration contention (observed at 70s-163s) now exhausts the budget and causes write loss, no longer writer-count storms, making FIFO queueing ineffective and bounded retry the matching remedy
